verdict.rationale: Daytona's pricing page points to a usage-based model: sandboxes spin up and shut down fast, and you "use what you need, when you need it," with included free compute. It never states per-second billing granularity or that you are charged only for actual compute consumed. missing for 10: explicit per-second billing documentation, published per-resource rates (vCPU/RAM/disk/GPU), clarity on whether stopped or idle sandboxes incur charges, independent corroboration of billing behavior.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can pay per second only for the compute a sandbox actually uses

citations.quote: Daytona lets you spin up sandboxes in milliseconds and shut them down just as fast. Use what you need, when you need it.
Use what you need, when you need it. $200 in free compute included.
